title: Grieg’s Wedding Day, abridged and complete
work: Wedding Day at Troldhaugen, Op. 65 No. 6
question: How does Grieg’s own pacing compare with Vetter’s in music both recordings actually share?
intro: Grieg recorded an abridged version of his piano piece in Paris on 2 May 1903; Harald Vetter’s complete performance dates from 2006. The historical disc is US public domain, and Vetter’s recording carries CC BY 4.0 at both IMSLP and Commons. Only the shared opening passage is mapped: Grieg 0:18–1:28 against Vetter 0:21.6–1:56.31, excluding the unreliable opening, cut ending and modern performance’s contrasting middle. Historical pitch instability and undocumented transfer choices limit exact tempo comparisons; the two whole-file durations are not comparable.

alignment.scope: Shared opening material only; the complete source recordings remain unedited. No whole-work tempo ratio.
alignment.note: An exploratory 4–94 / 5–120 second map had low-confidence opening points and a plateau near reference 90–91.5 seconds. Inspection against the measured 46/62-second and 74/98-second changes supported the shared passage but not the shortened ending. The published map excludes both uncertain ends; its remaining path was inspected and has no point below 0.8. No pitch transposition or audio edit was applied.
